claims.text: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can refine an inherited eutectic lamellar structure into a hierarchically heterogeneous ultrafine-duplex microstructure.
Producing this hierarchical ultrafine-duplex microstructure will simultaneously increase strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a lamellar dual-phase microstructure containing soft FCC and hard BCC or intermetallic phases.
The as-cast lamellar structure is coarse.
The as-cast alloy exhibits typical cast defects.
Cold rolling followed by annealing can produce an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure while retaining the inherited lamellar architecture in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The processed architecture has increased interphase-boundary density.
The heterogeneous processed microstructure promotes dislocation storage and effective strain distribution.
Severe cold rolling increases dislocation density.
Cold rolling promotes the formation of a high density of fine lamellar regions.
Subsequent annealing activates recovery and partial recrystallization, refining grains and lamellae and redistributing residual stresses.
The refined hierarchical microstructure enhances strain hardening by creating barriers to dislocation motion.
The hierarchical lamellar microstructure provides a constraint effect that improves mechanical response during deformation.
The hierarchical lamellar microstructure generates a microcrack-arresting mechanism.
Cold rolling and annealing increase the strength of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 relative to its unprocessed state.
Cold rolling and annealing retain or improve ductility relative to the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 baseline.
The processing route should improve both strength and ductility by approximately 10–20% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The expected effect applies to eutectic HEAs with inherent dual-phase lamellar structures but may not apply to single-phase HEAs or eutectics with substantially different phase chemistries.
The predicted response should hold during room-temperature quasi-static tensile testing at approximately 10^-3 s^-1 in an inert atmosphere.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis and falsification rule require an increase in ductility, whereas the predicted outcome also treats merely retaining ductility as an acceptable expected result. Under the stated falsification rule, retention without an increase would falsify the central hypothesis.
